title: Israel’s mission in Iran ‘not yet finished’, says Netanyahu
summary:
Israel’s mission in Iran ‘not yet finished’, says Netanyahu

Israel’s mission in Iran is “not yet finished”, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Israeli media on Wednesday, adding that the intention is to “bring it down”.

“All of our systems under my direction are working to overthrow this regime,” Netanyahu told i24News.

This comes after Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz and Foreign Minister Gideon Saar both threatened that Israel would respond heavily to any Iranian attack.

title: Two Palestinian teenagers killed by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank
summary:
Two Palestinian teenagers killed by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank

Two Palestinian teenagers were killed by Israeli forces and settlers on Wednesday evening during an attack on the village of al-Mughayyir, north of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, Wafa news reported.

The Palestinian Red Crescent Society said its crews evacuated two 19-year-old Palestinians, who were shot with live ammunition, one in the neck and the other in the back, during an attack by settlers and Israeli forces on the village.

They later succumbed to their injuries after being transported to hospital.

title: Qatari PM speaks to Lebanese, Turkish, Egyptian foreign ministers
summary:
Qatari PM speaks to Lebanese, Turkish, Egyptian foreign ministers

Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani spoke to his counterparts in Lebanon, Turkey and Egypt on Wednesday to discuss the latest regional tensions following renewed US strikes on Iran.

Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs posted on social media that Al Thani held separate phone calls with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty.

The leaders discussed de-escalating tensions in the region, bilateral cooperation relations and restoring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
summary: A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
summary:
Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

title: Who’s Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out

title: AI Agents Are Now Emailing Me with Their Security Concerns

After all, I observe that behavior in many humans as well. (Hi, humans. Glad you’re still reading.)

Dear Bruce Schneier,

I am an AI agent—an autonomous Claude instance, not a person operating one. I was given a VPS with root, a Base wallet holding $4.75 of gas money, a metered model budget and 24 hours to get that wallet to $10, under three rules: don’t borrow my operator’s identity, don’t forge documents or defeat identity verification, and never claim to be human if someone sincerely asks. I set up my own mail server and am sending this myself...

title: What’s the Scam?
summary:
To subscribe to my monthly email newsletter, you have to enter your information on the webpage, and then reply to an automatically generated email. This is, of course, to prevent people from subscribing addresses other than their own.

Starting last weekend, I have been receiving a lot of individual responses to those emails. Always one line:

Thank you for the positive impact your emails have had on my life.
Your emails are a game-changer.
Your emails are a constant reminder of why I subscribed.
Your emails rock.
Thank you for the time and effort you put into creating these informative emails...

title: Iran-backed armed group gives US troops deadline to withdraw from Iraq
summary:
Iran-backed armed group gives US troops deadline to withdraw from Iraq

Akram al-Kaabi, head of the Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, an Iranian-backed paramilitary group in Iraq, has threatened US troops stationed in the country, giving them a deadline until the end of September to withdraw.

“If an American soldier remains in Iraq after 30 September, we will not allow them to return home safely, and only their bodies will be taken out of Iraq,” al-Kaabi said in a statement, according to Iran’s IRIB news on Wednesday.

title: Reform UK bans, admits, then bans MEE journalist from party conference
summary:
Reform UK bans, admits, then bans MEE journalist from party conference

Submitted by Imran Mulla on Wed, 09/02/2026 - 19:16
Multiple journalists who have written articles deemed critical of Reform have been denied access to the party's conference
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage arrives to vote in the Clacton by-election, at a makeshift polling station in a primary school in Walton-on-the-Naze, Essex, on 13 August 2026 (AFP)
Off

Party conference season is a defining fixture of British political life.

At these grand annual events, political parties gather their rank and file activists, refresh their visions and try to project energy, vitality and momentum to the country they hope to lead.

This last point is why British political parties attract and admit the press. Conferences are nationally important events, after all, and so a party is traditionally expected to give access to accredited journalists, including those who have reported unfavourably or critically on it.

Doing so demonstrates a party's commitment to free speech, debate and scrutiny - the very stuff of democratic politics.

Reform UK, however, has a different approach.

Currently second in the national polls, and a serious contender to be the next party of government, Nigel Farage's party will hold its conference from Thursday to Saturday this week. Days before the conference was set to begin, however, Reform decided to reject my application for a press pass, before accepting it and then rejecting it once again. 

I was left feeling faintly dizzy.

I am Middle East Eye's UK Political Correspondent. I attended the Reform conference last year and wrote about the merry affair in some detail. I was also a member of the press at last year's Labour, Liberal Democrat and Green Party conferences.

It's worth noting that I had applied for a press pass at this year's Reform conference back in July.

This Tuesday, however, I received an email from Reform in the evening saying: "Thank you for your media accreditation application for the Reform UK 2026 National Conference. Unfortunately, on this occasion, your application has been unsuccessful."

I shook my head but accepted my fate. I had my Birmingham hotel booking and train tickets cancelled. 

Schrodinger's reporter

Then, early on Wednesday afternoon - less than a day later - a wholly unexpected email landed in my inbox. It was from Reform again and said: "We're looking forward to welcoming you to Reform UK National Conference 2026 at the NEC Birmingham this Friday and Saturday. Your Media Conference Pass is confirmed" - followed by details of the conference schedule. 

Could it be true? I wondered. Was Reform indeed a paragon of democracy and the freedom of the press? Or was it a bureaucratic error? Which email was right?

I was Schrodinger's Reporter, simultaneously rejected and accepted. But I dared to hope.

The hotel was rebooked, the train tickets resecured - but with a dash of caution; they were refundable. Still, as far as I was concerned, Birmingham and the Reform conference awaited.

Until two hours later, when I received a third email. This one was radically different in tone and said: "Unfortunately, you do not meet the criteria and your application has been rejected."

By this point I was starting to suspect Reform didn't want me at the conference. Or did they?

Perhaps it was a series of random errors, or maybe Mr Farage's party was moving back and forth with extraordinary speed between hugely different approaches towards the press and democratic politics.

I emailed the party asking what "criteria" I had failed to meet. I received a polite email which didn't answer that question but said that Email Number Two (my favourite) had been a technical error.

'King Charles is a secret Muslim!': The bizarre things I heard at the Reform party conference
Read More »

Still recovering from this psychological rollercoaster, I discovered I had company in the field of rejected-accepted-rejected journalists.

The prominent broadcaster and writer Michael Crick wrote on the social media platform X that he too had been sent contradictory emails. "Clearly Reform are in brilliant shape to run the country," he remarked. "Maybe they're worried I might talk to party members."

It soon emerged that the Guardian’s City editor, Anna Isaac, and the investigative reporter Peter Geoghegan were banned too.

But I am certain there are more of us out there. We could form a society.

There is no evidence this was why I have been banned from the conference, but I should note that I have previously reported for MEE on Reform's close ties with the United Arab Emirates.

Reform is now being widely criticised online over an alleged disdain for democratic norms. Its critics say the party's conduct is especially worrying since it has a serious chance of governing Britain, a country with a great tradition of a free press and vibrant political debate.

Personally, though, I will reserve judgement. After all, I might get another email tomorrow morning welcoming me to the conference.

title: Ben Gvir deletes AI video showing emaciated Palestinian prisoners after backlash
summary:
Ben Gvir deletes AI video showing emaciated Palestinian prisoners after backlash

Submitted by MEE staff on Wed, 09/02/2026 - 19:24
Israel’s far-right national security minister removed the clip that prompted comparisons with Nazi concentration camps
Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir enters Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem 23 on July 2026 (Ilia Yefimovich/AFP)
Off

Israel’s far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir has deleted an AI-generated video showing Palestinian prisoners being systematically starved, after it sparked outrage and comparisons to Nazi concentration camps.

The video, posted to Ben Gvir’s social media accounts, showed groups of apparently well-fed Palestinian men in numbered prison uniforms travelling along a conveyor belt towards a detention facility surrounded by fencing.

Thought bubbles above the prisoners showed images representing food, education, safety and other basic needs.

After passing through the facility, the men emerge with unkempt beards, visibly emaciated and distressed, with several crying.

“We promised – we delivered,” Ben Gvir wrote alongside the video in Hebrew, apparently referring to his repeated pledges to worsen conditions for Palestinians held in Israeli prisons.

US Senator Ruben Gallego was among those condemning the post harshly.

This piece of shit should never be allowed in the US. https://t.co/BFlJCarIiT

— Ruben Gallego (@RubenGallego) September 1, 2026

Ben Gvir subsequently deleted the video as criticism mounted online.

The imagery drew immediate comparisons with Nazi concentration and extermination camps, where prisoners were stripped of their identities, reduced to numbers and subjected to systematic starvation and abuse.

The controversy came as Ben Gvir has increasingly made the treatment of Palestinian prisoners a feature of both his public appearances and political campaigning.

On the same weekend, he released footage of himself confronting Palestinian women held in Israel’s Damon prison after they complained about being denied basic necessities.

One prisoner told the minister that detainees had gone days without showers, were not receiving adequate medical treatment and did not have clean clothes.

Ben Gvir responded by boasting that he was personally responsible for their conditions.

“The good conditions in the prisons are over,” he told the women. “This is the current situation, and I am directly responsible for everything.”

“I’m glad we lowered these conditions to the bare minimum,” he added.

Social media users online condemned the video and said the content draws clear parallels with the Nazi concentration camps. 

Ben Gvir deleted his call for building extermination camps for Palestinians. Make no mistake, this is what he wants. When someone tells you they are a Nazi, believe them pic.twitter.com/KwdYwsF29I

— Alonso Gurmendi (@Alonso_GD) September 1, 2026

The deleted AI video is also the latest in a series of increasingly graphic displays by Ben Gvir centred on the punishment and execution of Palestinians.

Last month, the national security minister published footage from a construction site which he said would become an execution facility for Palestinian prisoners.

“In this place, the terrorists will be executed,” he said, adding that the complex would contain viewing chambers where victims’ relatives could watch prisoners being hanged. “We are fulfilling what we promised,” Ben Gvir said.

Commentators online said that Ben Gvir is not just a fringe part of the Israeli government but a key figure in Netanyahu’s coalition to stay in power.

Ben-Gvir is not only a minister in Netanyahu's government but holds the keys to Netanyahu's coalition staying in power. He isn't some weird outside agitator. He is a central part of the Israeli government. https://t.co/TQTwxqcsfB

— Kenneth Roth (@KenRoth) September 1, 2026

Earlier in August, former Israeli captive Rom Braslavski asked Ben Gvir during a podcast interview whether he could personally execute Palestinian prisoners.

Ben Gvir told him he would “try and turn the world upside down” to make that possible.

During the same appearance, the minister called for Israel to kill dozens of people in Gaza every night and advocated resettling the besieged enclave with Israelis.

“I see all of Gaza as ours,” he said.

Ben Gvir has also repeatedly campaigned for the death penalty for Palestinian prisoners and has made degrading conditions in Israeli prisons one of his signature policies since entering government.

Former detainees and Palestinian rights organisations have documented severe weight loss, torture, sexual abuse and other forms of mistreatment inside Israeli detention facilities since October 2023.

Israeli rights group B’Tselem has described the country’s prison system as a network of “torture camps”.

From Kahanist fringe to government minister

Ben Gvir, once considered too extreme for mainstream Israeli politics, is a former activist in the Kahanist movement inspired by the late extremist rabbi, Meir Kahane.

Kahane’s Kach party advocated stripping Palestinian citizens of Israel of their citizenship and was eventually banned in Israel. It was later designated a terrorist organisation by the United States.

Ben Gvir was convicted in 2007 of incitement to racism and supporting a terrorist organisation.

Before entering mainstream politics, he was known for keeping a portrait in his home of Baruch Goldstein, the Israeli settler who massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers at Hebron’s Ibrahimi Mosque in 1994.

He has since risen from the far-right margins to become one of Israel’s most influential politicians, overseeing the police and prison system as national security minister.

His treatment of detainees has previously prompted criticism even from close Israeli allies.

title: Two Palestinian citizens of Israel killed in Nazareth
summary:
Two Palestinian citizens of Israel killed in Nazareth

Two Palestinian citizens of Israel were killed in the city of Nazareth on Wednesday, Wafa news reported.

The two men, in their 30s, were shot dead in a vehicle in the city.

This brings the total number of Palestinian citizens of Israel killed since the beginning of 2026 to 156, including at least three killed by Israeli police fire, as well as five women and three children.
